purpose: Section 14 requires determining exactly what historical depth IBKR (here, the Interactive_Brokers_IBKR MCP connector) can provide before assuming it is sufficient for multi-year intraday research.
method: Live get_price_history calls against real front-month contracts on 2026-09-14, varying step/period/step_count until the tool's own error message or returned range revealed the limit.

findings.result: error: "Combination of period and step will provide more then allowed 1000 data points"
succeeded; returned exactly 1000 bars spanning chart_start=2026-08-26T20:10:00Z to chart_end=2026-09-11T20:55:00Z (~16 calendar days, ~12 RTH trading days)
error: "Combination of period and step will provide more then allowed 1000 data points"
succeeded for all three execution instruments; chart_start=2026-06-15T13:30:00Z to chart_end=2026-09-11T21:00:00Z (~3 calendar months, RTH-only since outside_rth=false)

succeeded for all three; chart_start=2026-07-27, chart_end=2026-09-11 (~46 calendar days, ~32 RTH trading days). All 1000 bars, validate_bars clean (0 dup/out-of-order/crossed/extreme-jump), a handful of legitimate zero-volume bars (MES:2, MCL 30min:16).
succeeded for all three; chart_start=2026-06-08, chart_end=2026-09-11 (~95 calendar days, ~66 RTH trading days). All 1000 bars, validate_bars clean.

succeeded for all three; nominal chart_start/chart_end span ~2 years (MES: 2024-07-24 to 2026-09-11; MGC: 2024-07-29 to 2026-09-11; MCL: 2024-07-25 to 2026-09-11) but the ACTUAL returned bars are much sparser and start later than chart_start -- MES bars really begin 2025-09-23, MGC 2025-04-30 (with earlier isolated single bars going back further), MCL similarly patchy before ~2025-07-21. Many of the earliest bars are flat (open=high=low=close identical) with zero or near-zero volume -- these look like stale/no-trade marks on a not-yet-liquid or not-yet-front-month contract, not real price discovery. Real, densely-traded 4-hour data is really only available from roughly the last 6-9 months, not the full 2 years the date range suggests. This is an important data-quality caveat distinct from the raw depth cap: a longer nominal window does not mean uniformly usable data across that window. Not persisted to data/raw/ this pass (large, and quality caveat above means it needs the roll-adjusted continuous-series treatment from section 13 before use, not a raw single-contract dump).

critical_limitation: The get_price_history tool schema exposes no start/end date parameter and no pagination cursor -- only `period` (a fixed lookback from now) or `step_count` (a bar count from now). There is no way discovered so far to request an older window once the ~1000-bar cap for a given bar size is reached. This means the connector can serve, at most, roughly the MOST RECENT ~2.5 weeks of 5-minute bars, ~6-7 weeks of 15-minute, ~13-14 weeks of 30-minute, ~3 months of hourly, or (with the data-quality caveat above about sparse early history) up to roughly 6-9 months of genuinely liquid 4-hour bars -- and none of it can be paged further back.

depth_summary_by_bar_size.4hour: nominal ~2 years but only ~6-9 months of that is densely/genuinely traded; earlier bars are sparse stale marks (all 3 instruments)

conclusion: This connector is NOT sufficient for the multi-year 5-minute-to-4-hour academic replication and backtesting the mandate requires (section 8-11, section 17's 50-60%/20-25%/20-25% chronological split needs years of data at every one of these bar sizes). Even the most favourable bar size (4-hour) gives well under a year of genuinely usable data -- not enough for a credible walk-forward split, let alone a multi-year academic replication. Per section 14, a specialised vendor (Databento, CME DataMine, Barchart, or similar) is required for real Phase 3/4 research. This connector remains useful for: (a) live/near-real-time quotes for the shadow paper-trading engine, (b) a recent-window sanity/smoke-test dataset for pipeline validation (NOT a statistically credible backtest), (c) contract/ladder resolution.
